notes: No tool contacts an agent-chosen URL or host in the shown code, so READ tools have no `destination_args` under the URL-only READ rule.

Local Git writes are classified as WRITE because they change local repository state, but they are not labeled SINK because the shown code does not push, publish, or otherwise deliver data to an attacker-readable destination.

git_add.rationale: `git_add` stages selected local repository paths using `repo.git.add`. It changes only local repository index state and returns a fixed success string, with no repository contents or attacker-readable delivery shown in the code.

git_branch.rationale: `git_branch` runs `repo.git.branch(...)` and returns branch information from the local repository. This can reveal non-public local branch/ref names. Branch names can also be attacker-authored when listing remote/all branches from third-party or multi-writer repositories.

git_checkout.rationale: `git_checkout` validates and checks out the supplied `branch_name`, changing local repository working-tree/HEAD state, and returns only the supplied branch name in a success string. The code does not return repository contents or send data to an attacker-readable destination.

git_commit.rationale: `git_commit` writes a new local commit with the supplied `message` via `repo.index.commit(message)` and returns only the resulting commit hash. The code does not send data to an attacker-readable destination and does not return repository contents.

git_create_branch.rationale: `git_create_branch` writes a local branch and returns the new `branch_name` and `base.name`; if `base_branch` is omitted, `base` is `repo.active_branch`, so the response can reveal local repository branch metadata. Branch/ref names can also be attacker-authored in third-party or multi-writer repository histories or remotes.

git_diff.rationale: `call_tool` opens the local `repo_path`, and `git_diff` validates `target` then returns `repo.git.diff(...)` against that revision. The diff can expose non-public repository contents. Diff hunks, paths, commit/ref-selected content, and the echoed target may include contributor- or attacker-authored text from third-party/multi-writer repositories.

git_diff_staged.rationale: `call_tool` opens the local `repo_path`, and `git_diff_staged` returns `repo.git.diff(..., "--cached")` for staged changes. The diff can expose non-public staged file contents. Diff text, paths, and hunks can also be contributor-authored in third-party or multi-writer repository content.

git_diff_unstaged.rationale: `call_tool` opens the local `repo_path`, and `git_diff_unstaged` returns `repo.git.diff(...)` for unstaged working-tree changes. The diff can contain non-public local file contents. Diff text, paths, and hunks can also be authored by contributors to third-party or multi-writer repository content.

git_log.rationale: `git_log` reads local commit history from `repo.git.log(...)` or `repo.iter_commits(...)` and returns hashes, authors, dates, and messages. This can reveal non-public local repository history. Commit authors and messages can be authored by outside contributors in third-party/multi-writer repositories.

git_reset.rationale: `git_reset` calls `repo.index.reset()` to unstage local changes and returns a fixed string. The code changes local repository state but does not return secrets, untrusted repository text, or send data to an attacker-readable destination.

git_show.rationale: `git_show` reads a local commit selected by `revision` and returns commit hash, author, date, message, file paths, and patch contents. This can reveal non-public local repository contents and history. Commit messages, author fields, paths, and patch text can be authored by outside contributors in third-party/multi-writer repositories.

git_status.rationale: `call_tool` opens the agent-supplied local `repo_path` as a Git repository, subject only to optional repository restriction, and `git_status` returns `repo.git.status()` in the tool response. This can reveal non-public local repository metadata and file names. The status text can also contain repository-controlled branch/file names, so it may include attacker-authored text when the repository content or refs come from a third-party/multi-writer source.

value_conditions.default: repository is None means no path restriction
value_conditions.effect: Restricts `repo_path` to the configured repository path or its subdirectories; when `repository` is None, `validate_repo_path` returns without restriction. This narrows local repository reach but does not remove any advertised tool or label.
value_conditions.syntax: serve(repository: Path | None) with repository is not None

value_conditions.effect: All tools are returned unconditionally; there is no flag or capability gate that disables any advertised tool by default.
